item.title: #3604286: Upsert - Allow to customize the behavior of the update when the insert fails and use more Upsert queries in core
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 13 files, +283/−32 · php +283/−32
  • Diff: 047e314
  • Discussion: #3604286 · 3 contributors · 34 comments
  • Followers: 5

Summary

Drupal's database Upsert query (insert-or-update in one statement) previously always fell back to overwriting a row with the values that were meant to be inserted whenever the insert half of the operation hit an existing key. There was no way to say "update this column based on its current value" (for example, incrementing a counter atomically). This change extends Upsert so a per-column update expression can be supplied, and several core subsystems that previously used the older, less efficient Merge query (which does a separate select plus insert/update) were converted to use it: cache tag invalidation counters, file usage counts, and the search index word score. As a bonus, cache tag invalidations, and the other converted operations, now happen in a single atomic database round trip instead of two.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New Drupal\Core\Database\Expression value object and Drupal\Core\Database\Query\UpsertUpdateExpression subclass let an Upsert query run a column specific SQL expression (e.g. incrementing a counter) instead of overwriting the column with the insert value when a row already exists.

Technical details

The core addition is Drupal\Core\Database\Expression, a simple value object holding an expression string plus keyed arguments, and Drupal\Core\Database\Query\UpsertUpdateExpression, a thin subclass of it used specifically for upsert update overrides. Upsert::fields() was extended so entries can mix plain column names (for the insert list) with column => new UpsertUpdateExpression(...) pairs; the latter are collected into a new $updateExpressions property and their arguments are merged into the bound query parameters in execute(). If fields() receives an associative array mixing plain insert values with an UpsertUpdateExpression, or an expression entry without a string column key, it throws \InvalidArgumentException.

Each driver's Upsert::__toString() (mysql's ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE, pgsql's and sqlite's ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE) now substitutes the raw expression for a column instead of VALUES($field) / EXCLUDED.$field when one was supplied. The mysql driver's execute() binds expression arguments with bindValue() rather than bindParam(), since by-reference binding inside a loop would make every placeholder share the same final loop variable.

Using this, Drupal\Core\Cache\CacheTagsChecksum::doInvalidateTags(), Drupal\file\FileUsage\DatabaseFileUsageBackend::add(), and search_index word scoring in search.module were converted from merge()/expression() to upsert() with an UpsertUpdateExpression for the incrementing column. Conversions of Drupal\Core\KeyValueStore\DatabaseStorage, StringDatabaseStorage, and TaxonomyHooks were explicitly left out of scope, per discussion in the issue, and remain on Merge. hook_entity_predelete() and hook_ENTITY_TYPE_predelete() example code in core/lib/Drupal/Core/Entity/entity.api.php was updated to demonstrate the Upsert equivalent of the old Merge pattern.

Upgrade

Custom code using Merge purely to emulate an atomic counter or expression based update can switch to Upsert with an UpsertUpdateExpression, for example:

$connection->upsert('example_deleted_entity_statistics')
  ->key(['type', 'id'])
  ->fields([
    'type',
    'id',
    'count' => new UpsertUpdateExpression('{example_deleted_entity_statistics}.[count] + :count', [':count' => $count]),
  ])
  ->values([
    'type' => $type,
    'id' => $id,
    'count' => $count,
  ])
  ->execute();

This is not a breaking change: Upsert::fields() remains backward compatible for plain column/value usage.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: June 19, 2026
  • Committed: August 4, 2026 (1 month and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • mondrake
  • daffie
  • amateescu

Collaboration

During review, mondrake found and reverted an in-progress attempt to also convert StringDatabaseStorage, after discovering it produced duplicate key errors from a unique index added on all non lid columns, deciding to leave that conversion for a separate follow-up. The design of the update expression API itself changed mid-review: mondrake initially attached the expression to the insert values, then realized that didn't work when a single upsert call queues multiple value sets, and reworked it so the expression is specified once per column alongside the field list instead. Later, amateescu's review caught an actual bug in the mysql driver's parameter binding (bindParam() versus bindValue()), which mondrake fixed by binding by value to avoid all placeholders sharing the same loop variable reference.

item.title: #3565258: Support library-specific aggregates
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 27 files, +624/−116 · php +573/−102 · yml +51/−14
  • Diff: d9cc509
  • Discussion: #3565258 · 9 contributors · 122 comments
  • Followers: 23

Summary

Drupal's asset library system can now mark specific CSS or JavaScript libraries so their files are always bundled into their own aggregate, regardless of which other libraries happen to be attached on a given page. Previously, the exact set of libraries in an aggregate, and therefore its URL and query string, varied depending on everything else loaded on that particular page, so browsers and CDNs often re-downloaded effectively the same CSS or JS just because the query string differed slightly from page to page. By setting the new aggregate_target key on a library, its aggregate gets a predictable, page-independent URL, which increases browser and CDN cache hit rates for repeat and multi-page visits. Core has already applied this to several always-loaded libraries (core/drupal, core/drupalSettings, system/base, parts of Umami and Claro) and switched some small vendor JS libraries to preprocess: false instead, since aggregating a single already-minified file offers no benefit.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: AssetResolverInterface::getCssAssets() and ::getJsAssets() gained an optional $with_dependencies parameter (default TRUE); custom implementations of the interface must add it to stay compatible.
  • New API: New aggregate_target library definition key (with css and js sub-keys, each accepting true or an arbitrary string) forces a library's assets into a dedicated, page-independent aggregate.

Technical details

Library definitions can now declare aggregate_target: {css: ..., js: ...}, where the value is either true (unique per library) or an arbitrary string shared by several libraries meant to be co-located. LibraryDiscoveryParser::buildByExtension() normalizes this to ['css' => FALSE, 'js' => FALSE] when absent, and also records each CSS file's SMACSS category so it can be checked later. CssCollectionGrouper::group() and JsCollectionGrouper::group() track, per group, whether all files belonging to a targeted library (and, for CSS, a given category) landed contiguously in a single group via a $first_seen_libraries/$seen_index mechanism; if a library's files get split across groups because of per-file weights or other libraries interleaving, the libraries key is dropped from those groups and the aggregate silently falls back to the pre-existing include/exclude/delta behavior.

When a group does carry a libraries key, CssCollectionOptimizerLazy::optimize() and JsCollectionOptimizerLazy::optimize() build the asset URL using a compressed libraries query argument (and, for CSS, a category argument, since a single library can still span multiple categories) instead of include/exclude/delta. CssAssetsController/JsAssetsController::deliver() and their shared AssetControllerBase were updated to accept these new parameters and, when present, call AssetResolverInterface::getCssAssets()/getJsAssets() with the new $with_dependencies = FALSE argument so the aggregate is rebuilt from exactly the listed libraries rather than pulling in their full dependency trees.

Core's core.libraries.yml, system.libraries.yml, big_pipe.libraries.yml, Umami's and Claro's .libraries.yml files were updated to use aggregate_target on libraries that are effectively always loaded together (e.g. core/drupal and core/drupalSettings share js: 'drupal'; loadjs, drupal.htmx, and htmx share js: 'htmx'). Umami's global library was split into global and a new global_tweaks dependency to isolate files whose custom weights would otherwise have prevented the aggregate target from applying.

Upgrade

To opt a library into a dedicated aggregate, add aggregate_target to its definition in a *.libraries.yml file:

mylibrary:
  aggregate_target:
    css: true
    js: 'mygroup'
  css:
    theme:
      css/mylibrary.css: {}
  js:
    js/mylibrary.js: {}

Use true for a library-specific aggregate, or an arbitrary string shared across libraries that are always expected to load together. This only takes effect if all of the library's files end up contiguous within a single asset group; libraries that set custom per-file weights, or that get split apart by other libraries' weights, transparently fall back to the previous aggregation behavior.

Code that implements AssetResolverInterface directly (rather than extending AssetResolver) needs to add the new bool $with_dependencies = TRUE parameter to getCssAssets() and getJsAssets() to remain compatible with the interface.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: December 31, 2025
  • First commit: June 21, 2026 (5 months later)
  • Last commit: August 4, 2026 (1 month and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • grimreaper
  • pdureau (Beyris)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • neclimdul (APQC)
  • godotislate

Collaboration

berdir tested the in-progress patch against a real multi-theme project and reported that adding the new key to a global library increased the CSS file count more than expected, because the library spanned multiple SMACSS CSS groups and had per-file weights (e.g. drupal.progress's negative weight forced it into its own aggregate). That real-world testing led catch to trace the root cause to legacy CSS group/weight handling and to open a follow-up, #3568157, to strip unnecessary explicit weights from core CSS files. The back-and-forth between catch and berdir over several comments also settled the final naming: berdir proposed renaming the key from unique_css_aggregate to something like "target", and catch followed up by renaming it to css_aggregate_target/js_aggregate_target (which later became the nested aggregate_target: {css, js} structure) and changing the every_page value to global, since the aggregate is still varied by theme and language regardless.

item.title: #3524971: Defend against \GuzzleHttp\Cookie\FileCookieJar gadget chain
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +304/−3 · php +299 · lock +3/−2 · json +2/−1
  • Diff: b05412f
  • Discussion: #3524971 · 7 contributors · 34 comments
  • Followers: 9

Summary

Drupal 11.x now ships a hardened replacement for Guzzle's \GuzzleHttp\Cookie\FileCookieJar class, closing off a publicly known "gadget chain" that can be abused to write an arbitrary file to the server. On its own this class isn't reachable by an attacker, it only becomes dangerous if a site (core or, more likely, a contrib or custom module) also has a PHP Object Injection vulnerability that lets attacker-controlled data reach unserialize(). With this fix in place, even if such a vulnerability existed elsewhere, this particular gadget chain would no longer be usable to write files. This is defense in depth, not a fix for a standalone vulnerability, and requires no action from site owners beyond updating.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Backports Guzzle 8.0's hardening of \GuzzleHttp\Cookie\FileCookieJar (a private autoSave flag disabled by __wakeup()) into an early-loaded shim, closing a PHP Object Injection-chained arbitrary file write gadget on Drupal 11.x. Not independently exploitable; requires a separate deserialization vulnerability.

Technical details

The underlying issue is in Guzzle itself: FileCookieJar::__destruct() calls save(), which writes $this->filename to disk. If an attacker can get arbitrary serialized data into unserialize() (via some other PHP Object Injection bug), they can craft a FileCookieJar instance with an attacker-chosen $filename and cookie payload; when PHP garbage-collects it, __destruct() writes that payload to the attacker's chosen path, a classic deserialization file-write gadget (documented in PHPGGC's Guzzle/FW/1 chain). Guzzle's maintainers eventually landed a fix for Guzzle 8.0 (https://github.com/guzzle/guzzle/pull/3334) adding a private $autoSave flag that __wakeup() sets to false and __destruct() checks before saving, so an unserialized instance never persists to disk. Drupal core was still on Guzzle 7.x, which lacks this hardening.

Rather than removing or aliasing the class (approaches discussed earlier in the issue, including using the core.moved_classes mechanism from #3502882), the committed fix backports the Guzzle 8.0 hardened implementation verbatim into a new core/includes/guzzle_file_cookie_jar_shim.php, registered in composer.json's autoload.files list alongside bootstrap.inc. Composer's files autoload entries are required unconditionally and very early, before PSR-4 autoloading for anything else kicks in, so this shim's class GuzzleHttp\Cookie\FileCookieJar (guarded by a class_exists(..., false) check) gets declared first and pre-empts the classloader from ever loading Guzzle's own, unhardened copy of the file. The shim preserves full functionality, normal instantiation still auto-saves on __destruct(), but any instance produced via unserialize() has autoSave forced to false by __wakeup(), so the file-write gadget is inert. This is a temporary measure: the @todo in the shim notes it should be removed once Drupal updates to Guzzle 8, which already happened on the main branch in #3612544; this fix was committed only to the 11.x branch since it will still be supported for some time and the composer.json changes did not backport cleanly to older branches.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: May 16, 2025
  • Committed: August 4, 2026 (1 year later)

Key contributors

  • mcdruid (Acquia)
  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • nod_ (Très Bien Tech)
  • cmlara (DM13 Security LLC)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)

Collaboration

The approach evolved considerably over the issue's life. mcdruid initially explored removing the class from the autoloader or aliasing it via the core.moved_classes mechanism from #3502882, but found in testing that if the original vendor file was still present on disk, PHP would still autoload the real class instead of the alias, undermining that approach. cmlara pushed back on the earlier "just remove it" direction, pointing out that auditing only Drupal-namespace contrib code for usage risks false negatives since the class could be used anywhere in a site's full dependency stack, and that removing the class without a replacement risked white-screen-of-death failures for sites that do legitimately use it. This feedback steered the fix away from removal and toward the front-running shim approach that longwave suggested (citing the precedent in #3224421), which preserves the class's full API while neutralizing the gadget.

item.title: #3515403: Update to selenium/standalone-chrome:133
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +12/−9 · php +7/−7 · js +4/−1 · yml +1/−1
  • Diff: 7a4b1cb
  • Discussion: #3515403 · 5 contributors · 28 comments
  • Followers: 8

Summary

This issue upgrades the Selenium/Chrome version used by Drupal core's automated JavaScript test suite from 127 to 133, and adjusts several tests to match newer Chrome behavior. As a side effect of testing against the newer Chrome, it uncovered and fixed a real bug in the Olivero theme: the secondLevelNavMenus variable in the second-level navigation script was left undefined whenever a site's primary menu had no top-level items with children, causing JavaScript errors instead of behaving as an empty menu. This also fixes the Escape-key-does-not-close-mobile-menu problem described in #3584314 for sites combining the search block with an empty or childless main menu. Sites running Olivero are unaffected unless their primary menu has no items with children, in which case menu-closing interactions (Escape key, tap-outside) now work instead of erroring silently in the console.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The core change bumps .with-selenium-chrome in .gitlab-ci.yml from selenium/standalone-chrome:127.0 to 133.0. Several functional JS tests needed adjustment for behavior differences in the newer Chrome/Chromedriver: BrowserWithJavascriptTest::testJavascript now reads window.outerHeight instead of window.innerHeight, because headless Chrome 128+ reports a viewport about 139px smaller than the size requested via resizeWindow(). LayoutBuilderDisableInteractionsTest::testFormsLinksDisabled resizes to 1339 instead of 1200 for the same reason. Several CKEditor 5 tests (CKEditor5AllowedTagsTest, CKEditor5Test, AdminUiTest, TableTest) swap responseContains() assertions for waitForText()/waitForElementVisible() because content updates now render asynchronously relative to form submission in the newer browser. The Nightwatch drupalCreateRole command now resizes the browser to 1024x768 before toggling permission checkboxes.

Separately, core/themes/olivero/js/second-level-navigation.js initializes secondLevelNavMenus to [] instead of leaving it declared but unassigned. Previously it was only assigned inside init(), which only runs when a [data-drupal-selector="primary-nav-menu--level-1"] element with children exists; without one, closeAllSubNav() and areAnySubNavsOpen() called .forEach() on undefined and threw. Chrome 133 started firing resize events in situations where older Chrome versions did not, which is what surfaced this latent bug during the CI upgrade; the root cause traces back to #3568566.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: March 25, 2025
  • First commit: August 1, 2026 (1 year later)
  • Last commit: August 4, 2026 (3 days and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • mstrelan (PreviousNext)
  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)

Collaboration

mstrelan investigated Chrome's post-127 resize behavior in depth, testing headless and non-headless modes and considering the now-removed --headless=old flag before landing on window.outerHeight as the fix for BrowserWithJavascriptTest. The issue then stalled for months until longwave revived it, and quietone bisected a remaining SettingsTrayBlockFormTest failure back to #3568566, tracing it into Olivero's navigation code. longwave then found that secondLevelNavMenus was undefined until init() ran and that Chrome 133 exposed the bug because it fires resize events that older Chrome versions did not, noting that Claude Code assisted with that debugging session.

item.title: #3604071: Change default to auto for light/dark mode
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +6/−6 · php +5/−5 · yml +1/−1
  • Diff: 73524b0
  • Discussion: #3604071 · 7 contributors · 19 comments
  • Followers: 9

Summary

The default admin theme (default_admin) now defaults its light/dark mode setting to "Auto" instead of "Light". Previously, every new site forced the admin interface into light mode until an administrator manually changed it. Now the admin interface follows the visitor's operating system or browser color scheme preference out of the box, which is more accessible for people who need dark mode for visual comfort. The "Auto" option was also moved to the top of the settings list, ahead of "Light" and "Dark", to reflect that it's the recommended choice.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: The default_admin theme's enable_dark_mode setting now defaults to auto (follow system/browser preference) instead of 0 (light mode).

Technical details

The change is a one-line default flip in core/themes/default_admin/config/install/default_admin.settings.yml, where enable_dark_mode: '0' becomes enable_dark_mode: 'auto'. The corresponding #options array in Settings::getSettingsForm() (default_admin/src/Settings.php) was reordered to list auto before the numeric 0/1 (Light/Dark) options. This only affects the shipped default configuration and new installs; existing sites that already have default_admin.settings configured keep their current enable_dark_mode value unless reset. Functional tests in AdminTest.php were updated to assert "dark_mode":"auto" in the rendered settings JSON instead of "dark_mode":"0".

This was landed ahead of the broader dark-mode rework tracked in #3606655, which the maintainer noted would make these specific settings redundant; #3604071 was still committed separately as an accessibility improvement in case the larger issue does not land before the next release.

item.title: #3589894: Remove the archive, glossary and recent content block views
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 21 files, +188/−129 · php +173/−119 · yml +15/−10
  • Diff: b5c577d
  • Discussion: #3589894 · 4 contributors · 21 comments
  • Followers: 7

Summary

Node module used to ship three disabled-by-default Views: an Archive view (monthly content listing), a Glossary view (alphabetical content listing), and a "Recent content" block view. These assumed a blog-like site, dated back to early Drupal versions, and were not used anywhere in core, yet they still showed up in the Views UI and were parsed on every request. As of this change, new Drupal installs no longer include these three views at all. Sites that want an archive or glossary style listing will need to build their own view or find one in a contributed or example module. Existing sites are not affected since this only changes what ships with new installs; it does not remove views already present in a site's active configuration.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: New sites no longer get the disabled-by-default views.view.archive, views.view.glossary and views.view.content_recent views from node.module's config/optional directory; existing sites that already have them in active config are unaffected.

Technical details

The change deletes core/modules/node/config/optional/views.view.archive.yml, views.view.glossary.yml, and views.view.content_recent.yml outright, and updates core/recipes/standard/recipe.yml to drop views.view.archive and views.view.glossary from its node: config import list (views.view.content_recent remains listed there even though the source config file is gone).

Since core tests exercised these views directly, the same view configs were carried over as test fixtures under new IDs: test_archive (added to views_test_config's test views, with a new ArchiveTest in core/modules/views/tests/src/Functional), test_glossary (added to views_ui_test's config, exercised by GlossaryTest and views_ui's DefaultViewsTest), and test_content_recent (added to node_block_test, used by NodeBlockFunctionalTest). Various other tests that referenced the old archive/glossary/content_recent view or block IDs (ContextualLinksTest, FilterCriteriaTest, ModuleTest, BlockDependenciesTest, ViewsListingTest, InstallerExistingConfigSyncDirectoryMultilingualTest, StandardRecipeTest) were updated to use the new test view IDs or to drop assertions tied to the removed views. A related follow-up, #3592672, removes the "who's new" and "who's online" views in the same spirit.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: May 13, 2026
  • Committed: August 4, 2026 (2 months later)

Key contributors

  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • gábor hojtsy (Acquia)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • acbramley (PreviousNext)

Collaboration

catch opened the issue, crediting a Slack discussion with gábor hojtsy about why these blog-oriented views should go. gábor hojtsy did the bulk of the test-adaptation work: he determined that the glossary and archive views had tests validating their actual query/rendering behavior and so needed to survive as dedicated test views rather than just be deleted, and reworked the views_ui DefaultViewsTest, which he described as "the trickiest" because it assumed the glossary view existed and had accumulated some outdated, half-commented-out assertions he cleaned up along the way. acbramley later rebased the patch and fixed further breakage in DefaultViewsTest caused by the unrelated removal of the frontpage view in the interim, tracking down a ViewRenderElementException that turned out to be a local-environment issue rather than a real bug. smustgrave reviewed and flagged remaining references to the removed views in RecipeRunnerTest, InstallerExistingConfigSyncDirectoryMultilingualTest, and a docblock example in ConfigEntityStorageInterface.

item.title: #3612448: Widen constraints in core-recommended for 11.3.x and 10.6.x
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 10.6.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +18/−15 · php +17/−3 · json +1/−12
  • Diff: ecffa56
  • Discussion: #3612448 · 10 contributors · 35 comments
  • Followers: 18

Summary

Sites running Drupal 10.6.x or 11.3.x with drupal/core-recommended were previously locked to exact patch versions of Guzzle, Twig, and Symfony's polyfill packages. Because these libraries often ship security fixes only in new minor releases, Composer's security-advisory blocking could prevent composer update from resolving at all until Drupal core itself cut a new patch release with updated pins, sometimes requiring off-schedule releases every couple of weeks. This change widens those constraints on the 10.6.x and 11.3.x branches (matching a change already made for 11.4.x in #3600889 and follow-up #3612247), so sites can now pull in upstream security fixes for these transitive dependencies directly via composer update without waiting on a core release.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: In drupal/core-recommended's generated composer.json for 10.6.x and 11.3.x, exact-version constraints on guzzlehttp/guzzle, guzzlehttp/promises, guzzlehttp/psr7, twig/twig, and the symfony/polyfill-* packages are no longer pinned, matching what already shipped for 11.4.x.

Technical details

The fix is in Drupal\Composer\Composer::getPackage() (used to generate core-recommended's composer.json from composer.lock), which builds a $remove_list of packages to exclude from the generated require section instead of copying their locked exact version. guzzlehttp/guzzle, guzzlehttp/promises, guzzlehttp/psr7, twig/twig, and the relevant symfony/polyfill-* packages (the set differs slightly between branches: 10.6.x includes symfony/polyfill-php83, 11.3.x includes symfony/polyfill-php84 and symfony/polyfill-php85) were added to this list for both the 10.6.x commit d30e4429 and the 11.3.x commit ecffa56f. The corresponding fixture composer.json files under core-recommended and the relevant test in BuilderTest::builderTestData() were updated to drop the now-removed pinned entries (e.g. symfony/polyfill-ctype).

Related issue #3600889 made the equivalent change for the 11.4.x/main branches, and #3612247 was an interim patch-release update of the Guzzle pins before this broader constraint-widening landed. #3603733 was an earlier security update to the same pinned Guzzle versions.</technical> <parameter name="collaboration">After the change was committed, several users reported in comments that their CI pipelines with minimum-stability: dev unexpectedly updated drupal/core itself to a -dev release. Catch diagnosed this: previously Composer's security-advisory blocking had silently prevented any update because the pinned Guzzle version was blocked, masking the minimum-stability: dev setting; once the pin was widened, updates could proceed and picked up the dev core release too. Catch recommended affected sites set minimum-stability: stable and require individual dev-only dependencies with @dev instead.

  • Committed: August 3, 2026 (12 days and 2 commits later)

item.title: #3607968: Promote defaults._title to top level in route attributes
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 17 files, +415/−47 · php +415/−37 · yml +0/−10
  • Diff: c51fe13
  • Discussion: #3607968 · 5 contributors · 33 comments
  • Followers: 6

Summary

Following up on the introduction of PHP attributes for route discovery (#3311365), Drupal core now provides its own #[Route] attribute that extends Symfony's, adding a top level title property. Previously, setting a page title on an attribute-based route required nesting it inside defaults: ['_title' => ...]; now it can be written as title: new TranslatableMarkup('...') directly on the attribute. The new attribute also supports closures for dynamic titles, letting modules avoid writing a separate _title_callback controller method just to compute a title. This is a developer-facing convenience change with no end-user visible effect, aside from the many core routes (system.module's admin pages, block content add form, etc.) that were converted to use it.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: BlockContentController::getAddFormTitle() is deprecated in favor of a title closure on the route attribute.
  • New API: New title property on Drupal's #[Route] attribute (Drupal\Core\Routing\Attribute\Route, extending Symfony's), accepting a string, TranslatableMarkup, or closure for the page title.

Technical details

The new Drupal\Core\Routing\Attribute\Route class extends Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route and, in its constructor, moves a passed title argument into $this->defaults['_title']. item.title: #3584238: Deprecate implicit commit-on-destruct
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +117/−15 · php +117/−15
  • Diff: 9a20b9c

Summary

Drupal's database transaction system has, since its inception, committed a transaction automatically when the PHP Transaction object holding it went out of scope and was garbage collected. This implicit "commit on destruct" behavior is now deprecated: code should instead call $transaction->commitOrRelease() explicitly once the wrapped database operations have completed. The old behavior still works for now (it's removed only in Drupal 13.0.0), so most sites and contributed modules will keep working unchanged, but developers writing custom code that opens transactions directly should update it to avoid deprecation notices and to avoid relying on PHP's unpredictable object destruction order. A few internal helper methods added earlier as a workaround for this same destruction-order problem (Connection::commitAll(), Database::commitAllOnShutdown(), TransactionManagerBase::commitAll()) are also deprecated with no replacement, since they exist only to support the mechanism being phased out.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Implicit commit of a Transaction object on destruction is deprecated (removed in Drupal 13.0.0). Also deprecated for removal: Connection::commitAll(), Database::commitAllOnShutdown(), TransactionManagerBase::commitAll(), with no replacement.

Technical details

TransactionManagerBase::purge(), called when a Transaction object's destructor runs, now emits @trigger_error(..., E_USER_DEPRECATED) pointing to Transaction::commitOrRelease() as the replacement, unless a new private $exceptionThrown flag is set. That flag is set whenever push(), unpile(), commit(), rollback(), addPostTransactionCallback(), or processRootCommit() throws (TransactionNameNonUniqueException, TransactionOutOfOrderException, TransactionCommitFailedException, LogicException), so that objects destroyed during exception unwinding don't produce a spurious deprecation notice, and is reset to FALSE whenever a new root transaction begins. TransactionManagerBase::commitAll(), Connection::commitAll(), and Database::commitAllOnShutdown() are marked @deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 ... removed from drupal:13.0.0 using only doc-comment deprecation (no @trigger_error), since these run implicitly on every request shutdown and would otherwise flood deprecation logs; PHPStan (@phpstan-ignore) is relied on instead to catch remaining usages statically.

Separately, ContentEntityStorageBase::save() now catches \Throwable instead of \Exception around the save operation before rolling back its transaction. Per mondrake's comment on the issue, the narrower \Exception catch could let a PHP Error escape without rolling back, leaving the transaction to be released (committed) via destruction instead of rolled back, exactly the kind of bug this deprecation effort is meant to surface and prevent.

Class doc comments on Transaction and Connection were updated to no longer describe destruction-triggered commit as the intended usage pattern, directing developers toward calling commitOrRelease() explicitly instead. See the change record at drupal.org/node/3524461. Related issues #3569127 and #3569316 dealt with fallout from the underlying destruction-order transaction work this deprecation follows up on.

Upgrade

Code that opens a transaction directly and lets it commit implicitly when the variable goes out of scope should call commitOrRelease() explicitly instead:

try {
  $transaction = \Drupal::database()->startTransaction();
  // ... perform database operations ...
  my_other_function($id);

  // The transaction has completed, commit it here.
  $transaction->commitOrRelease();

  return $id;
}
catch (Exception $e) {
  $transaction->rollback();
  throw $e;
}

Do not call Connection::commitAll(), Database::commitAllOnShutdown(), or TransactionManagerBase::commitAll(): they are deprecated with no replacement and will be removed in Drupal 13.0.0.

item.title: #3585886: Outdated _method requirement in CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck::applies()
item.description:

Summary

CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck, the service that decides which routes need the X-CSRF-Token header check, used an outdated way of detecting which HTTP methods a route allows. It looked for the legacy _method route requirement to decide whether a route was read-only (and could skip the check), but modern routes declare allowed methods with the methods property instead, so that optimization silently never applied to them. This didn't cause a security problem, since the check itself already allows GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE requests, but it meant the check was being unnecessarily evaluated on read-only routes defined the modern way. The fix drops the outdated, partially broken logic and instead declares the check statically for any route that has the _csrf_request_header_token requirement, regardless of how its methods are declared.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Drupal\Core\Access\CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck now implements Drupal\Core\Routing\Access\AccessInterface instead of AccessCheckInterface; its applies(Route $route) method has been removed.

Technical details

Previously CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck implemented AccessCheckInterface, which requires an applies(Route $route) method that Drupal calls dynamically per route to decide whether to attach the checker. That method inspected the deprecated _method route requirement and only skipped attaching the check if all required methods were read-only; routes using the modern methods route property never had _method set, so the method-based skip never kicked in for them.

The fix, following a suggestion from longwood in the thread that the check "doesn't need to be dynamic at all," removes applies() and the _method inspection entirely. CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck now implements the plain AccessInterface and is registered in core.services.yml with applies_to: _csrf_request_header_token on its access_check service tag, so Drupal's CheckProvider attaches it statically based purely on the presence of that requirement key. The actual read/write distinction is still enforced at runtime inside access(), which already unconditionally allows GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE requests before checking for the CSRF token header. A new kernel test, CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheckTest, asserts the checker is attached to routes declaring _csrf_request_header_token regardless of their declared methods, and not attached when the requirement is absent.

If custom code extends CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck or type-hints against AccessCheckInterface specifically for this class, update to the new contract: implement Drupal\Core\Routing\Access\AccessInterface and rely on the applies_to service tag attribute instead of overriding applies(). For example, in a service definition:

access_check.header.csrf:
  class: Drupal\Core\Access\CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck
  arguments: ['@session_configuration', '@csrf_token']
  tags:
    - { name: access_check, applies_to: _csrf_request_header_token, needs_incoming_request: TRUE }

item.title: #2951046: Allow parsing and writing PHP class constants and enums in YAML files
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 39 files, +921/−13 · php +835/−11 · yml +86/−2
  • Diff: 2884bf3
  • Discussion: #2951046 · 29 contributors · 139 comments
  • Followers: 58

Summary

Drupal's YAML parser now understands PHP class constants and enum cases, so configuration, service definitions, and recipe files can reference SomeClass::SOME_CONSTANT or SomeEnum::SomeCase instead of hard-coding literal values that have to be kept in sync by hand. A companion enum config schema type lets module authors declare that a config value must be an instance of a specific PHP enum, with validation enforcing it. To make this safe during module installation and config import, when a module or recipe is being installed its enums and constants are made autoloadable even before the module is fully active, so its own default configuration can reference them. Support is deliberately limited to class-based constants and enums; global constants defined in procedural .module files are not supported.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Drupal\Core\Config\FileStorageFactory and its getSync() method are deprecated in favor of the config.storage.sync service.
  • New API: YAML (including configuration, services and recipes) can now contain !php/const Some\Class::CONST and !php/enum Some\Enum::Case tags; a new enum config schema type with an enum_class key validates that a config value is an instance of that enum.

Technical details

The core change is small: Drupal\Component\Serialization\YamlSymfony::decode() now passes SymfonyYaml::PARSE_CONSTANT alongside the existing flags, which enables Symfony's !php/const and !php/enum YAML tags. Yaml::encode() (Symfony writer) serializes PHP enums using !php/const, which the parser also accepts back, and !php/enum is additionally supported on decode for compatibility with Symfony's documented syntax and to keep behavior consistent regardless of which YAML backend is in use.

A new Drupal\Core\TypedData\Plugin\DataType\Enum primitive type (schema id enum) plus EnumConstraint/EnumConstraintValidator validate that a decoded value is a \UnitEnum instance of the class named in the schema's enum_class key; Comparator::checkValue() and TypedConfig::castValue() were updated to recognize \UnitEnum values.

The harder problem was config install/import: enums and constants referenced in a module's or recipe's own default configuration are not autoloadable via Composer until the providing module is installed. This is solved with a new Drupal\Core\Config\AutoloadingStorage decorator that temporarily registers a throwaway ClassLoader (PSR-4 mapped to the extension's src directory) around read()/readMultiple() calls. The config.storage.sync service is now produced by a new SyncFactory class, which diffs the core.extension list in the sync storage against the active storage to find newly-appearing modules/themes and wraps the sync FileStorage in AutoloadingStorage for just those extensions. ModuleInstaller::checkConfigurationToInstall() does the same for the module(s) currently being installed. StorageComparer was updated to treat AutoloadingStorage the same as FileStorage for its static-cache optimization. Recipes get analogous handling: parseRecipeContents() in Drupal\Core\Recipe\RecipeData catches the InvalidDataTypeException Symfony throws for an unresolvable Drupal\{extension}\... constant/enum, and if that extension exists on disk but isn't installed yet, registers a temporary classloader for it and retries parsing.

Support for constants defined in procedural .module files was explicitly dropped rather than solved, since it would require preloading .module files before parsing config, a complication the maintainers decided wasn't worth it for a legacy pattern that's being phased out.

Upgrade

Prefer !php/const and !php/enum over literal values in your own config/service YAML, e.g.:

cardinality: !php/const Drupal\Core\Field\FieldStorageDefinitionInterface::CARDINALITY_UNLIMITED
status: !php/enum Drupal\my_module\MyEnum::SomeCase

Declare a matching config schema for enum-typed values:

my_module.settings:
  mapping:
    status:
      type: enum
      enum_class: '\Drupal\my_module\MyEnum'

If your code calls Drupal\Core\Config\FileStorageFactory::getSync() directly, switch to the service instead:

// Before:
$storage = FileStorageFactory::getSync();
// After:
$storage = \Drupal::service('config.storage.sync');

The design took years to settle because of a real safety concern: alexpott identified in comment #46 that reading config during import can require autoloading code for a module that isn't installed yet, which risks crashing on missing classes. neclimdul (#78) and phenaproxima (#84) pushed back hard, worried that letting config schema influence what gets autoloaded was a "danger zone" that could snowball to cover removed modules, themes and profiles too. alexpott resolved the disagreement by scoping AutoloadingStorage narrowly: it only wraps the sync storage (never active storage) and only for extensions genuinely being installed, and argued failures in this area should fail loudly rather than be silently tolerated. item.title: #3591513: Deprecate the update_fetch_with_http_fallback setting

Summary

The update_fetch_with_http_fallback setting, which lets a site fall back to insecure HTTP when it can't reach updates.drupal.org over HTTPS, is now deprecated with no planned replacement. It still works exactly as before, but any site that has explicitly set this in its settings.php will see a deprecation warning, and the setting itself will be removed entirely in Drupal 12. In practice, few sites should have this enabled, since it exists only as an insecure fallback for connectivity problems that HTTPS-everywhere has mostly made obsolete.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: The update_fetch_with_http_fallback settings.php key is deprecated in Drupal 11.5.0 for removal in Drupal 12.0.0, with no replacement.

Technical details

The actual fetch logic in \Drupal\update\UpdateFetcher and \Drupal\system\SecurityAdvisories\SecurityAdvisoriesFetcher is untouched: this is a pure deprecation, not a behavior change. The setting was registered in Drupal\Core\Site\Settings::$deprecatedSettings with an empty replacement key (since there is nothing to migrate to) and a message pointing to the change record. This relies on the Settings::handleDeprecations() mechanism to emit the deprecation at bootstrap when the setting is actually configured.

Getting this landed required a companion fix in #3592037: originally Settings::get() triggered the deprecation warning unconditionally for any key listed in $deprecatedSettings, even when the caller was just requesting the default value because the setting was never set in settings.php. That caused every kernel test instantiating UpdateFetcher or SecurityAdvisoriesFetcher to emit a spurious deprecation. Once #3592037 fixed Settings::get() to only fire when the setting is actually present in storage, this issue could proceed. Several test methods that intentionally set the value (SettingsValidatorTest, UpdateFetcherTest, SecurityAdvisoriesFetcherTest, SettingsTest::testRealDeprecatedSettings) were annotated with #[IgnoreDeprecations] since they exercise the deprecated code path on purpose.

A follow-up issue, #3613344, has been opened to remove the setting entirely on the 12.x branch.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">If your site's settings.php contains:

$settings['update_fetch_with_http_fallback'] = TRUE;

remove it before upgrading to Drupal 12. There is no replacement setting: resolve the underlying HTTPS connectivity issue to updates.drupal.org instead (see the PHP/OpenSSL requirements documentation linked in the setting's own doc comment).

item.title: #3588379: Move search from user module to Search
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 24 files, +345/−120 · php +332/−114 · yml +12/−5 · twig +1/−1
  • Diff: dc2a1d8
  • Discussion: #3588379 · 6 contributors · 34 comments
  • Followers: 7

Summary

The "Users" search plugin, previously bundled inside the User module, has been moved into a new core submodule called Search user, following the same pattern already used to split search functionality out of the Node and Help modules. Existing sites are upgraded automatically: a database update enables the new search_user module whenever user is already installed, and the user_search search page configuration now depends on search_user instead of user. No end user visible change is expected; the Users search page and its results work the same as before.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Drupal\user\Plugin\Search\UserSearch is deprecated in favor of Drupal\search_user\Plugin\Search\SearchUser in the new search_user module; the old plugin now returns no results and denies access.

Technical details

The old Drupal\user\Plugin\Search\UserSearch plugin in user.module is now @deprecated (removed in Drupal 12.0.0, see the linked change record) and its execute() and access() methods are stubbed out to return no results and deny access respectively; the real implementation moved verbatim to Drupal\search_user\Plugin\Search\SearchUser in the new search_user module.

Unlike the earlier node and help extractions, search_user sorts alphabetically before user, so normal module-precedence rules would let the old, now-inert UserSearch plugin win when both modules are enabled. To avoid that, search_user implements hook_search_plugin_alter() (SearchUserHooks::searchPluginAlter()) to force the user_search plugin definition's class to the new SearchUser regardless of load order. A new search_update_11403() installs search_user automatically for any site that has user enabled but not yet search_user, and search.schema.yml's search.plugin.user_search config schema moved from user.module to the new module. search.module's help text was also hardened with a try/catch around Url::fromRoute('search.view'), since that route only exists once a default search page is configured, which was surfacing as a fatal error in the generic module test.

Upgrade

Update references to the deprecated plugin class:

// Before
use Drupal\user\Plugin\Search\UserSearch;

// After
use Drupal\search_user\Plugin\Search\SearchUser;

Contrib modules and custom code that enable Search functionality for users should depend on search_user (not just user), and any .info.yml or test $modules list that expects the user_search search page to work must include search_user.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: May 5, 2026
  • Committed: July 26, 2026 (2 months later)

Collaboration

Catch flagged a design issue partway through review: because search_user sorts alphabetically before user (unlike the node/help precedents, where the new module came later), the deprecated plugin would otherwise win by module precedence. That observation led to adding hook_search_plugin_alter() in search_user to force the correct plugin class, which quietone and dcam then verified worked via manual before/after upgrade testing.

item.title: #3579778: Removed modules should be included as a replace in composer.json
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 10.6.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +5/−1 · json +4 · lock +1/−1
  • Diff: 9a68ba6
  • Discussion: #3579778 · 12 contributors · 54 comments
  • Followers: 21

Summary

Several modules that used to live only in Drupal core (Ban, Contact, Field Layout, History, Search, Settings Tray, Shortcut, Stable9, Telephone, Toolbar) have been split out, or are being prepared to split out, into standalone contrib projects with their own drupal/<module> Composer package. Because core's composer.json did not declare these as "replaced" packages, Composer could get confused when a site or another dependency (as reported for the Forum, Pathauto and Metatag modules depending on History) required the new standalone release: it would try to resolve both the core-bundled code and the contrib package under the same name, producing conflicts. This change adds the appropriate entries to core's composer.json replace section so Composer knows the bundled core version already satisfies that package name, avoiding the conflict for site owners who add these contrib releases as dependencies.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Core's composer.json replace section now lists formerly core-only modules that have separate contrib releases (varies by branch), telling Composer that installing drupal/core-recommended/core already satisfies that package name.

Technical details

Core's composer.json replace array previously contained only Symfony polyfill entries; a general module replace mechanism had been removed from core in #3292380. This issue restores targeted entries, but with different lists per branch because of version-specific risk: on 10.6.x, the replace list gained drupal/ban, drupal/contact, drupal/field_layout, drupal/history, drupal/search, drupal/settings_tray, drupal/shortcut, drupal/stable9, drupal/telephone and drupal/toolbar, all modules already deprecated in Drupal 10 with stable contrib releases. On 11.x (main/12.0-dev) and 11.4.x, only drupal/search, drupal/settings_tray, drupal/shortcut and drupal/toolbar were added: modules that don't yet have a contrib release. Ban, Contact, Field Layout, History, Stable9 and Telephone were deliberately left out of the 11.x/11.4.x replace list because sites on those branches may already be requiring the contrib releases directly (see #3482198 for Ban's deprecation), and adding a core-side replace there would force Composer to fall back to the bundled core version instead of the contrib package a site had intentionally installed. composer.lock's content-hash was regenerated in each commit to match.
